reader.self_description: Claude (Opus 5.5) as join-pass reader TJ01: read every claim card in full from join-queue.json and the deposit ranges listed under read; evidence phrases copied by script with substring assertion; judgments are readings, not verifications of truth.

change: premise corrected, channel kept: #1570 gives Theophrastus as heir to the library 'by Aristotle's will' and the Aristotelian corpus as reaching us through his library; #1671 (Appendix C, item 9, citing T1570-04) attributes the handing-over to Strabo three centuries on, says the will names no books and no text states how they passed, and keeps the one channel through which both corpora reach us; development order agrees with registration dates
sets.basis: The #1671 knowledge-object item cites #1570's thesis (T1570-04) for the single transmission channel and corrects the will-inheritance premise #1570 stated with it.

evidence.phrase: so the two texts share one transmission channel
Aristotle's will names no books, and no text states how they passed

sets.name: Succession as authorship
sets.basis: Both read the received succession (Plato to Aristotle; the Theophrastan node) as the mechanism by which the corpus is partitioned into persons, which #1605 §17 names 'succession as authorship'.

evidence.phrase: succession is the **mechanism of the corpus**
the transmission form §17 called *succession encoded as authorship*

sets.name: What the deletion of the Crimson Hexagon destroyed (#1426)
sets.basis: Two claims of one erratum on the repository deletion: what deletion erases is the instrument, and what is rebuilt is a different traversal; distinct claims of one account.

evidence.phrase: deletion erases most deeply is not the idea but the instrument
What comes back will not be the same poem.

the transform-view editions beyond the first
